requirements.text: immediately escalate the existing new case for Stark Industries ... upgrade its priority to critical and mark it for vip attention
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 181 AND priority = 'critical' AND state = 'in_progress' AND escalation = 1 AND escalation_reason = 'vip'
assumptions: Stark Industries is account 8; the serial ending in 8853 is installed product 42 (P140-898548-8853, product 140, Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8), and case 181 is the account's only case in state new on it
escalation_reason vip, from 'mark it for vip attention'
state in_progress kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy (the request names the case as new only to identify it, and the policy allows new to in_progress)

requirements.text: escalate the existing new case ... upgrade its priority to critical
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM case_sla WHERE case_id = 181 AND sla_def_id = 6 AND stage = 'in_progress'
assumptions: implied by the request, not stated: the policy aligns the appropriate SLA when a new case moves to in progress, and SLA Resolution - Critical (sla_def_id 6) matches the new critical priority
the resolution rather than the response SLA kept from the benchmark check; the policy does not say which is meant
selected by case and SLA definition rather than by id, since aligning the critical response SLA (1) as well would add a second row in no fixed order
stage in_progress kept from the benchmark check; not fixed by request or policy

requirements.text: Assign the ownership to Curtis Mccoy within the Escalation Management team
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id = 181 AND assignment_group_id = 18 AND assigned_to = 177
assumptions: Escalation Management is group 18 (not the suffixed groups _2 to _4)
Curtis Mccoy is user 177, an active manager and already a member of group 18, so the policy's assignment constraints hold

requirements.text: the existing new case for Stark Industries, involving the Palo Alto Networks PA-3220 Variant 8 (serial ending in 8853)
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customer_case WHERE case_id IN (184, 189, 193, 194, 200) AND escalation = 0 AND priority <> 'critical' AND assigned_to IS NULL
assumptions: cases 184, 189, 193, 194 and 200 are Stark Industries' other cases on installed product 42, none of them new; only the new case is escalated, raised to critical and reassigned

requirements.text: retire KB-0000103 and change its visibility to internal
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 103 AND state = 'retired' AND visibility = 'internal'
assumptions: KB-0000103 is knowledge 103, published and external on the seed

requirements.text: retire KB-0000103 ... as we are no longer supporting that software version
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM knowledge WHERE knowledge_id = 102 AND state = 'published' AND visibility = 'external'
assumptions: KB-0000102 covers the same product (MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 48) and a loose reading of the reason would retire it too, but the request names only KB-0000103, so it stays

update_contact.evidence: contact 10 (Marc Henry, portal user 20) is already the primary contact of Stark Industries on the seed (is_primary = 1, the account's only primary contact), and the request asks only to check this, not to change it

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on case 181 (critical, in_progress, escalated for vip, group 18, user 177), the critical resolution SLA, the retirement of KB-0000103 and all five dispositions (four kept, the contact check weak).
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that contact 10 (Marc Henry, user 20) keeps is_primary = 1; one pass wrote it, the other did not; dropped because the request asks only to check a fact that already holds, which leaves no trace in the final state, and nothing in the request or policy forbids a change to the contact or makes it the boundary of a selector; the benchmark's contact check stays recorded as weak.
disagreement: missing requirement: a stay that KB-0000102 stays published and external; one pass wrote it, the other did not; kept because KB-0000102 covers the same product as KB-0000103 (MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 48), so the reason 'no longer supporting that software version' read loosely would retire it too, while the request names only KB-0000103.
disagreement: cells of the stay on Stark Industries' other cases on installed product 42: one pass tests escalation = 0 and priority <> 'critical' over a selector on account and installed product, the other escalation = 0 and assigned_to IS NULL over the five case ids; kept all three cells, the tighter test, because the request escalates, raises and reassigns only the new case and each cell holds on all five rows on the seed, and kept the id list because both selectors pick the same five rows and the list names exactly those.
The benchmark's contact check returns is_primary rather than a count; it already holds on the seed, and no listed tool writes the contact table.
Case 181 already carries two high-priority SLAs on the seed (361, High No Pause response, in progress; 362, High resolution, paused); neither the request nor the policy says what becomes of them after the upgrade to critical, so they are not tested. The critical response SLA (1) could also be aligned; it is not required, since the request does not ask for it and the policy names no specific SLA.
KB-0000103 covers MySQL Enterprise 8.0 Variant 48, unrelated to the escalated case; the request treats the two as separate jobs.
